newsitem.title: USA: Heavy rain puts California on flood alert.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain puts California on flood alert.

text.p: Heavy rain over northern California caused mudslides and swelled rivers on Saturday, raising fears of a new round of flooding after devastating floods earlier this month.

The second Pacific storm this week brought part of a hillside crashing down on U.S. Highway 50 in the Sierra Nevada mountains, forcing the closure of one of the main routes from northern California to Nevada.

Pat Miller, spokeswoman for the California Department of Transportation, said the mudslide was "pretty massive", covering a 600-foot (180 metre) to 800-foot (240 metre) stretch of the highway in a layer of mud and rocks up to 70 feet (20 metres) deep. "There's a mass of mud and trees and rocks out there on the roadway," Miller said.

The slide, near the town of Kyburz, damaged or destroyed three houses and swept two or three cars into the river alongside, Miller said. She said the occupants of the vehicles were rescued and there were no reports of deaths or injuries.
Highway 50 reopened last week after being closed for 17 days because of the New Year's floods. Miller could not estimate how long it would remain closed this time.
A number of other roads in northern California were closed for a time on Saturday because of mudslides or flooding.

The rain came at a bad time for California, which has not yet recovered from New Year's floods which damaged thousands of homes, inundated wide areas of farmland and caused at least $1.5 billion of damage. Some areas were still waterlogged.

Residents of flood-prone areas sandbagged homes and bought supplies as they anxiously watched swirling brown rivers rise again. Flood warnings were in effect for the Russian and Napa rivers in northern California's wine country, which were expected to go above flood stage in places later on Saturday.

With the ground saturated after one of the wettest months on record, the new rain ran off into streams, swelling rivers. The new storms were particularly cruel for flood victims who had just returned to clean up their homes only to face the threat of renewed flooding.

Steve Martarano, a spokesman for the California Office of Emergency Services, said there was rain in the forecast for the next five days. "There's a lot of concern with a lot of levee areas," he said.
State officials were especially worried about levees along the San Joaquin River in central California, which were weakened by the floods earlier this month.
Crews have worked furiously to repair breaks in the levees and to shore up weak spots using truckloads of rock.

Officials had a difficult task managing flood storage space in reservoirs, many of which were nearing capacity. They had to keep some storage space empty in case of new storms, but heavy releases of water from the reservoirs could aggravate flooding downstream.

Many residents of the Guerneville area, which lies along the Russian River about 50 miles (80 km) north of San Francisco, either packed up their possessions and moved to higher ground on Friday or sandbagged their homes and bought supplies in anticipation of flooding.
